name: Open Behavioral Styles Inventory (OBSI-32)
description: 32-item open-source Likert screening inventory for four behavioral styles — Dominance, Influence, Steadiness, and Conscientiousness — inspired by Marston's (1928) DISC model. Eight items per style, interleaved in a fixed D-I-S-C rotation. This is an original instrument written for this study; it is not any of the commercial DISC assessments and reproduces none of their proprietary forced-choice items. The style with the highest mean score is the candidate primary style; a second style within 0.30 of the primary is reported as a blended profile (e.g. DC, SI).
citation: Marston, W. M. (1928). Emotions of Normal People. Kegan Paul, Trench, Trubner & Co. (OBSI-32 items constructed for this study; the four-style model is used as the theoretical frame only.)
license: OBSI-32 items © this study, released CC-BY. The DISC four-factor model is public domain; 'DiSC' and 'Everything DiSC' are trademarks of John Wiley & Sons and are not used here.

dimensions.label: Dominance (D)
dimensions.description: Direct, decisive, results-driven; takes charge, comfortable with conflict, impatient with delay

dimensions.label: Influence (I)
dimensions.description: Enthusiastic, persuasive, sociable, optimistic; people-oriented, seeks recognition, acts on impulse

dimensions.label: Steadiness (S)
dimensions.description: Patient, calm, loyal, supportive; prefers stability and harmony, dislikes being rushed or surprised

dimensions.label: Conscientiousness (C)
dimensions.description: Analytical, precise, systematic, cautious; fact-based, high standards, follows procedure, reserved

items.text: I take charge of situations quickly and decide what needs to happen next.
I energize a room and enjoy being the center of attention.
I stay calm and even-tempered even when others are agitated.
I check facts and details carefully before drawing a conclusion.
I care more about getting results than about how people feel about the process.
I persuade people best through enthusiasm and personal warmth rather than facts.
I prefer a stable, predictable routine over frequent change.
I prefer to follow established procedures and standards rather than improvise.
I am comfortable confronting people directly when something is wrong.
I make friends easily and strike up conversations with strangers.
I am a patient listener and let people finish before I respond.
I would rather be accurate than fast.
I get impatient when discussions drag on without reaching a decision.
I tend to see the bright side and expect things to work out.
I stay loyal to the people and organizations I am part of, even through difficult times.
I ask a lot of questions before committing to a plan.
I enjoy competition and am motivated by winning.
I prefer talking through ideas with others over working through them alone.
I put the needs of the group ahead of my own.
I keep my feelings to myself and rely on logic in decisions.
I would rather act boldly and correct course later than wait for certainty.
I enjoy recognition and praise for my contributions.
I dislike being rushed and prefer to work at a steady, consistent pace.
I hold my work and the work of others to a high standard of quality.
I push back hard when someone tries to control what I do.
I act on impulse and go where the excitement is.
I avoid conflict and try to keep relationships harmonious.
I am cautious about risk and want to understand what could go wrong.
I set demanding goals and expect others to keep up.
I would rather inspire people toward a goal than manage the details of getting there.
I need time to adjust before I commit to a new way of doing things.
I prefer to work independently on tasks that require precision and focus.
